supersedes.reason: Frozen EDI ver.8 entity returned HTTP 403 before any mechanism outcome was computed. V2 preserves the biological hypothesis, response, model family, validation, direction and thresholds; only the accessible weather revision and explicit snow field are updated.

question: Does year-to-year snowfall immediately before breeding interact with island snow-retention habitat to explain deviations from the otherwise shared regional Adelie population trajectory?

response.annual_growth: log1p(N_i,t) - log1p(N_i,t-1) for adjacent annual censuses
response.extinction_rule: retain the positive-to-zero extinction transition; exclude zero-to-zero post-extinction intervals
response.local_deviation: island annual growth minus the mean annual growth of all other eligible islands in the same interval

scientific_source.title: Daily weather averages for Palmer Station, Antarctica (1989-2023) ver 9

predictor.annual_metric: number of October calendar days immediately before the November census with numeric Precipitation Snow (cm) > 0
predictor.trace_rule: non-numeric trace code T is not counted as a numeric observation or positive day
predictor.missingness: a year is eligible only when at least 25 October days have numeric snow-precipitation observations
predictor.standardization: z-score eligible-year October snow-precipitation-day counts within each training fold

static_island_modifier.name: fraction of breeding habitat classified as suboptimal/snow-prone
static_island_modifier.role: previously published physical-habitat vulnerability modifier; not independent fresh static evidence

primary_model.leave_one_year_out: withhold all island observations from one interval end-year; predictor scaling is training-only
primary_model.support_rule: interaction coefficient < 0 AND full model leave-one-year-out RMSE < null RMSE

falsification: full model does not improve leave-one-year-out RMSE
fewer than 15 eligible annual intervals remain after the 25-day completeness rule
interpretation_boundaries: Palmer Station snowfall is a regional/local weather proxy and not direct snow depth on each island.
The published habitat modifier is prior-known and its static decline association is not counted as new evidence.
The interaction test does not establish causality.
Post-extinction Litchfield zero-to-zero intervals are excluded by design.
